Locate trees and score grow-in / fall-in risk per segment

Source: R/risk.R
assess_risk.Rd

Every metric is computed against both conductor bounds from conductor_profile() (identical where the conductor is measured).

Usage

assess_risk(
  rasters,
  profile,
  segments,
  tree_ws_m = 5,
  min_tree_m = 3,
  phase_offset_m = 3,
  growth_m = 0,
  under_line_m = 6,
  wire_zone_m = 10,
  clearance_target_m = 4.6,
  cover_min_m = 2,
  min_support = 6,
  structures = NULL,
  structure_mask_m = 8,
  min_encroach_m2 = 5,
  coverage_m = wire_zone_m,
  min_observed = 0.75
)

Arguments

rasters

Output of corridor_rasters().

profile

Output of conductor_profile().

segments

Output of segment_lines().

tree_ws_m

Local-maximum window for treetop detection (metres).

min_tree_m

Minimum treetop height.

phase_offset_m

Horizontal offset of the outer conductors from the mapped centreline (OSM maps the right-of-way centreline, not each phase).

growth_m

Growth allowance added to tree heights (e.g. expected growth over a trim cycle).

under_line_m

Horizontal distance from the centreline within which canopy counts as "under the conductors". Canopy there is scored as grow-in; treetops there are excluded from the fall-in count so the two are not double-counted.

wire_zone_m

Half-width of the wire zone for canopy cover.

clearance_target_m

Target vertical clearance between canopy and the lowest conductor. The default 4.6 m (15 ft) is a common utility clearance-at-time-of-work target; it is not the NERC FAC-003 minimum vegetation clearance distance, which is smaller.

cover_min_m

Canopy height counted as cover.

min_support

A CHM cell counts as canopy only if at least this many cells of its 3 x 3 window are >= cover_min_m. Removes 1-2 cell features (unmapped single poles, stray conductor returns classified as vegetation) that would otherwise appear as trees directly under the line. It also trims crown edges slightly.

structures

Optional sf points of support structures (e.g. OSM pole/tower nodes and the line's own vertices, which OSM mappers place at structures). Canopy within structure_mask_m is zeroed so poles, H-frames and crossarms are not scored as trees under the line.

structure_mask_m

Mask radius around each structure (metres); should cover the structure's across-line width. Masked cells are excluded from cover and clearance and trees there are not scored, but they count as observed for frac_observed (a known structure, not a data gap).

min_encroach_m2

Canopy area inside the clearance envelope needed to call a segment grow-in (guards against single-cell artefacts).

coverage_m

Half-width of the band over which LiDAR coverage is measured (frac_observed). Set it to the corridor half-width so that voids beside the line, where strike trees stand, count too.

min_observed

A segment whose observed share of either the coverage_m band or the under_line_m zone is below this, and that would otherwise be "none", is tiered "no data": absence of risk cannot be claimed where the LiDAR did not see the ground.

Value

A list: segments (sf, one row per segment) and trees (sf treetops). Columns ending _lo / _hi use the lower / upper conductor bound. frac_observed and frac_observed_under are the shares of the grid cells within coverage_m and under_line_m of the segment (not past the line's ends) with an observed terrain and canopy value; cells off the edge of the data count as unobserved, structure-masked cells as observed (known structures, not gaps). priority is the tier under the optimistic (upper) bound, i.e. what holds even if the conductor is as high as plausible; priority_lo is the pessimistic tier, which saturates wherever canopy stands under a bounded span (the lower bound is only ~5 m above ground). Tiers are "grow-in", "fall-in", "no data" (no risk found, but coverage below min_observed) and "none". A grow-in or fall-in finding stands even at low coverage, though unseen cells could hide a more severe tier. confidence is "measured" (conductor observed over at least half the segment), "robust" (same tier under both bounds), "bound-dependent" or "low coverage" ("no data" under both bounds). encroach_*_m2 is the canopy area under the conductors inside the clearance envelope. Rows are ordered by what holds even under the optimistic (upper) conductor bound - encroachment, then strike trees - then by the same metrics under the lower bound.
